result.title: LIFT: Local Metric Alignment and Foundation-guided Propagation for Few-shot Depth Completion
result.summary: Few-shot depth completion aims to recover dense metric depth from sparse measurements using only a small number of target-domain annotations, offering a favorable balance between annotation cost and model adaptation. We propose LIFT, a framework that harnesses both depth and feature priors from a frozen pretrained monocular depth estimation (MDE) foundation model for few-shot depth completion. Specifically, LIFT first estimates local scale and shift parameters on a coarse grid and interpolates them into smooth, dense parameter fields, providing a spatially adaptive metric depth initialization. It then progressively refines this initialization through multi-scale depth propagation guided by foundation features. Finally, a lightweight residual decoder combines multi-level foundation features with propagation correction to refine the metric depth. Extensive experiments on NYUv2 and KITTI-DC demonstrate that our proposed method achieves state-of-the-art few-shot performance. The source code will soon be released.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出 LIFT，用冻结的单目深度基础模型先验做少样本深度补全：先在粗网格上估计局部尺度与平移并插值为稠密参数场，再用基础特征引导的多尺度传播和轻量残差解码器细化度量深度。
AI.relevance_reason: 属少样本稠密深度回归任务，虽复用预训练特征，但没有推理期状态生成、证据获取或停止决策等与 LVR 相关的机制，多尺度深度传播只是特征级上采样细化，与 latent 推理状态更新无可核查的具体联系。
